title: Ivo and the Sigil
premise: Astrid Joubert has spent her whole life in the valley of Vell, a pocket country erased from every map and sealed against magic, where her hedge-witch mistress keeps her useful and invisible. When a dying courier presses a sigil-marked map into her hands, Astrid learns Vell is a prison built by its own founders—and that she, as the last heir of the sealing bloodline, is the only one who can open the door out before the moon's thirteenth turn locks it forever. Hunted by the Warden who guards the seal and shadowed by a found family of exiles who each gave up something to escape other sealed places, Astrid must choose between the safety of smallness and the terrifying freedom of inheritance. In the end she rewrites the sigil rather than breaking it: Vell opens, magic returns gently to the valley, and Astrid—no longer apprentice, no longer invisible—walks out through the door and leaves it unlocked behind her.
about_author: Mara Sterling is a former cartographer's assistant who grew up in three countries and belongs to none of them, a rootlessness that fuels her fiction about doors, borders, and belonging. She writes at dawn in a converted lighthouse on the northern coast, where she lives with her partner, an ill-tempered cat named Marginalia.

chapters.title: The Valley That Isn't
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Establishes daily life in Vell: gathering herbs for Mistress Odile, mending charms that never quite work because magic cannot follow past the ridge. Astrid confesses she memorizes maps of places she'll never see. Emotional beat: quiet ache of confinement disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A bleeding man collapses at the river ford, muttering about 'the thirteenth turn.' He presses a leather map case into her hands and dies whispering her family name—Joubert—a name she's never been allowed to ask about. Emotional beat: shock; the world intrudes.

chapters.title: What Odile Knew
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid hides the map and confronts Odile, who goes pale at the name Joubert and forbids her to leave the valley. That night Astrid finds Odile burning letters bearing the same wax sigil as the map. Emotional beat: betrayal; the mentor becomes a warden.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with an interlude from the dying courier's journal tucked in the map case. The journal reveals Vell was sealed deliberately by twelve founders, one per moon-turn, and a thirteenth key remains unaccounted for. Emotional beat: dread mixed with exhilarating purpose.

chapters.title: Running Toward the Ridge
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She flees at night with the map, bread, and Odile's second-best cloak. Crossing the ridge, she feels magic brush her skin like weather for the first time—overwhelming, half-terrifying. Emotional beat: vertigo of freedom; grief for what leaving costs.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Every Map
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Outside, she discovers roads literally refuse to lead anywhere: travelers circle back, signs rearrange. The map is the only true path, and it demands a toll at each waypoint. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Debt
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At a drowned village she meets Tam, a laconic ferryman exiled from another sealed place called Corvel, who recognizes the sigil-work. He agrees to guide her in exchange for a promise: if she opens Vell, she'll try to open his home too. Emotional beat: first fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam explains the Warden—an entity made of the founders' guilt that hunts anyone carrying a founder's key. He lost his sister to it. Astrid realizes the map is warming against her chest, responding to her blood. Emotional beat: shared grief becoming trust.

chapters.title: The Wayhouse of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They shelter at a wayhouse run by Sefa, a sharp-tongued cook who feeds strays of every kind, and her adopted crew of misfits. For one night Astrid experiences found family: laughter, a full table, a bed. Emotional beat: warmth she didn't know she was starving for.

chapters.title: The Warden's Shadow
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The Warden arrives wearing the faces of everyone Astrid has failed, offering to let her go home if she surrenders the map. She refuses; the wayhouse burns; the company scatters. Emotional beat: guilt, and the discovery that she can't unknow herself anymore.

chapters.title: Salt and Second Chances
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Regrouping on the coast, Sefa reveals she once held a key of her own and chose comfort over courage; she won't watch Astrid make the same retreat. She gives them her boat. Emotional beat: redemption passed forward like an inheritance.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Beneath a sunken library they find records of the twelve founders—including Astrid's grandmother, who hid the thirteenth key inside a living bloodline rather than an object. Emotional beat: awe; Astrid stops being a runaway and becomes an heir.

chapters.title: What the Key Costs
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam realizes opening Vell will also unseal Corvel—and whatever the founders imprisoned there. He must decide whether his hunger for home outweighs his fear. Emotional beat: the theme of inheritance as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: Odile at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Odile intercepts them—not to stop Astrid but to beg her to, revealing she was the twelfth founder's apprentice and helped build the prison out of love for its victims' peace. Emotional beat: reconciliation without agreement; two kinds of mercy collide.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The moon enters its final cycle; the map's waypoints begin to seal themselves shut one by one. The company races across a landscape actively erasing itself. Emotional beat: urgency; no road back now even if she wanted one.

chapters.title: The Face in the Sigil
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the penultimate waypoint the Warden traps Astrid alone and shows her the truth: the seal exists because the founders' magic, freed, once devoured a generation. It offers her the same bargain Odile took. Emotional beat: temptation at its most reasonable.

chapters.title: Company of the Unsealed
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Tam, Sefa, Odile, and the wayhouse strays arrive to stand with her—not to fight the Warden but to witness her choice, each naming aloud what they lost to sealed places. Emotional beat: found family fully realized; courage borrowed and returned.

chapters.title: The Door in the Mountain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Climax begins: Astrid reaches the door beneath Vell's heart and finds it doesn't want a key—it wants an author. Her blood can break the seal or rewrite it. The Warden and Odile both plead their cases as the moon reaches fullness. Emotional beat: the weight of choice distilled.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Seal
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Climax. Instead of shattering the sigil, Astrid amends it: magic may enter Vell by invitation, not conquest, and no door may be locked from the outside again. The Warden, its purpose fulfilled differently, dissolves into ordinary moonlight. Emotional beat: triumph through wisdom, not force.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Revised
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Vell wakes: hedges bloom out of season, Odile's charms finally hold, villagers greet magic like an old friend returning from a long voyage. Tam weeps at word that Corvel's seal is loosening too. Emotional beat: belonging achieved, not granted.

chapters.title: Apprentice No More
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Odile formally ends her apprenticeship and asks instead to be taught. Astrid takes up the courier's unfinished rounds, delivering letters between valleys that were never supposed to touch. Emotional beat: inheritance accepted and transformed.

chapters.title: The Unlocked Door
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, coda. One year later, Astrid stands at the mountain door—which she has left permanently ajar—and watches new arrivals walk in: refugees from other sealed places, drawn by rumor of a valley that says yes. She lights a lamp for whoever comes next. Emotional beat: belonging as an open door, kept open on purpose.
